column1: # A public chronology, for GE-T13's fourth clause (SMYSL-2.4 §5.5).
# Columns, tab-separated: earlier, later, relation, note.
#   relation  `before`   the earlier value's extent may not start after the later one's ends.
#             `disjoint` the stronger claim: the earlier thing had finished before the later
#                        one began, so the two extents may not overlap at all.
#   A line with two columns means `before`. A line with three may omit the note.
# Every order below is a matter of public record and checkable without this repository: the
# note names the events so a reader can disagree with the pair rather than with the engine.
# What is authored here is the *selection*, and it is chosen to be awkward — approximate and
# uncertain values, unspecified digits, seasons, intervals, open ends, a negative year and a
# `Y`-year (whose year this build bounds to 32 bits, so the universe's own age is refused) — rather than to pass.
# --- the year-precision spine, antiquity to now ---------------------------------------------

column4: Caesar assassinated; the Western Roman Empire ends
…; the King James Bible is printed
…; On the Origin of Species is published
the UN Charter enters into force; the UDHR is adopted
the UK's EU referendum; the UK leaves the EU
Eagle touches down; Armstrong steps off it
VE Day; the surrender of Japan is announced
the two world wars, at year precision
the same two, at day precision
William I reigns; Richard I reigns
the Hundred Years' War; the Thirty Years' War

column1: 18XX
19XX

column4: a year inside a century, and the century after it

column1: # Only `before` within one year, and that is this build's answer to OQ-71(b) rather than a
# weakness of the pair: EDTF fixes no hemisphere, so a season is its whole year here and spring
# and autumn of 1918 have the same extent. Across a year boundary the order is recoverable.

column4: the summer of 1944 and the spring of 1945
the American Civil War opens; it ends
the Wall Street crash; Roosevelt's first inauguration

column1: # `before` only, deliberately. This build gives `1920~` the extent of `1920` (OQ-71(a): a
# qualifier is not a width), under which these would be disjoint — but claiming so would make
# the chronology fail the day a width is introduced, for a reason that is not about order.

column4: two approximate years a century apart
two uncertain years, the order not in doubt
the archaic and the classical, both approximate

column1: # --- ends nobody recorded: not decidable, and that is reported rather than passed -----------

column4: everything up to 1800, then a year after it
a year, then everything from 1900 onwards
the oldest known stone tools precede the ides of March
